# Recorded Connect 4 comparison results

Recorded 10-10-2026 19:52 (Europe/Paris) from public TAG commit
 d65ad79f04992e238663c37c812dc2c5f6ce7ff2 (clean checkout reported by user).
Used the existing authorised disposable build, Java 21.0.12 and its dependency
classpath. The reference checkout was not modified. Generated by
[ExportConnect4.java](../../tools/java-comparison/ExportConnect4.java), validated by
[Connect 4 comparison test](../games/connect4/java_comparison.rs).

The compiler generated the class and exited successfully but printed the existing
AccessDeniedException while closing a Netty dependency archive. Export and Rust
comparison both completed successfully. No permission/configuration workaround.
The disposable build is the previously compiled baseline; this task did not
rebuild the framework or independently reverify the reference commit.

## Corpus and limits

3,268 prefixes across 128 complete games, with repeated initial/early positions:
2,950 distinct configuration/history pairs. Four configurations (width, height,
target): (7,6,4), (5,4,3), (10,8,6), (3,2,3). For each, 32 games: trial 0 always
chooses the first action, trial 1 the last, other trials use java.util.Random with
seed 1000+trial to select a legal action. Rust replays recorded columns; matching
engine random seeds is not assumed. Corpus has 62 seat-0 wins, 34 seat-1 wins,
32 draws and all four winning directions. All prefixes include both player copies.

This is bounded evidence, not exhaustive default-board enumeration, all possible
histories, invalid inputs, target-one semantics or performance measurement.
Approved Rust target-one behaviour is tested separately because it corrects the
source behaviour. Rust resource limits and impossible-target rejection are also
separate tests. The independent Rust oracle covers broader experimental values.

## Schema v1

The first line records schema/version/provenance. Each subsequent TSV row has:

1. Width,height,target, comma-separated.
2. Recorded selected columns, comma-separated; empty for initial state.
3. Full-state signature.
4. Player-0 copy signature.
5. Player-1 copy signature.

Each signature has 14 pipe-separated fields: x-major board (`.`, `x`, `o`),
historical actor, next actor (-1 if finished), move count, turns within round,
completed rounds, first player, game status, both player results, both scores,
ordered actions (column:landing-row), ordered winning cells (x:y).

Cumulative completed turns are a separate Rust query; the within-round value is
what the source exposes as its turn counter. Nonacting Rust views offer no moves;
recorded copies enumerate the current actor's actions. Tests compare visible
facts and validate observer-specific offers separately.
